plan.hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided superiority)
assumptions: One-sample comparison against null mean μ₀ = 0
t-test is two-tailed in computation, but directional hypothesis is one-sided; alpha allocation to upper tail only
scientific_notes: Effect size (Cohen's d) = (μ − μ₀) / σ = 0.2 / 0.5 = 0.4, a small-to-medium effect
One-sided test at α = 0.05 uses one-tailed critical value; power inversion seeks minimum integer N meeting target power 0.80 under the non-centrality parameter t-distribution
R pwr package one-sample t-test function will be used for verification

answer.summary: For a one-sample one-sided t-test detecting a mean increase of 0.2 units (SD = 0.5, Cohen's d = 0.4) at significance level α = 0.05 with target power 80%, the minimum integer sample size is 41 participants. This design achieves 80.86% power, exceeding the 80% target. The preceding design (n=40) achieves 79.97% power, confirming that n=41 is the minimum integer meeting the criterion.
answer.method: Analytic inversion using R pwr package (pwr.t.test): one-sample one-sided t-test, d = 0.4, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "greater". Continuous solution n ≈ 40.03 rounded up to integer 41. Power verified at both n=41 and preceding n=40.
assumptions: Standard deviation σ = 0.5 is known or accurately estimated
One-sample comparison against null mean μ₀ = 0
One-sided test (H₁: μ > 0) with full alpha = 0.05 allocated to upper tail
No missing data, attrition, or non-compliance
limitations: Sample-size formula assumes t-distribution exactly; validity improves with n > 30 (satisfied here)
Does not account for potential dropout or protocol violations
Effect size (0.2 units) must be clinically/practically meaningful in the specific context
Assumes the SD estimate is stable across the full sample

executions.code:
# Load pwr package for power analysis
library(pwr)

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
d <- mean_diff / sd  # Cohen's d = 0.4

cat("=== One-Sample One-Sided t-Test: Sample Size for 80% Power ===\n")
cat("Effect (mean increase):", mean_diff, "units\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd, "units\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", d, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test with type="one.sample", alternative="greater" for one-sided test
# pwr.t.test uses: n = NULL (we solve for n), d, sig.level (alpha), power, alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("Continuous solution from pwr::pwr.t.test:\n")
cat("n =", result$n, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer for practical sample size
n_min <- ceiling(result$n)

cat("Minimum integer sample size:", n_min, "participants\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at n_min
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  n = n_min,
  d = d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", power_achieved, "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm n_min is the minimum
if (n_min > 1) {
  power_prev <- pwr.t.test(
    n = n_min - 1,
    d = d,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = "greater"
  )$power
  
  cat("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", power_prev, "\n")
  cat("Difference:", power_achieved - power_prev, "\n")
}

# Return the results as JSON
results <- data.frame(
  metric = c("sample_size", "achieved_power", "preceding_sample_size", "preceding_power"),
  value = c(n_min, power_achieved, n_min - 1, power_prev),
  unit = c("participants_total", "probability", "participants_total", "probability")
)

cat("\n=== RESULTS ===\n")
print(results)

# Output JSON
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = power_achieved, unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "preceding_sample_size", value = n_min - 1, unit = "participants_total"),
      list(metric = "preceding_power", value = power_prev, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
))
